caption: The drawing depicts a single laboratory apparatus, specifically a Bunsen burner, centered on a plain, light beige background. The main body of the Bunsen burner is cylindrical and rendered in shades of gray, suggesting it is made of metal. The base is wide, circular, and flat, helping the apparatus to stand upright and stable; the base is shaded with darker grays to simulate shadow and dimensionality. Extending upward from the base, the vertical tube is tall and cylindrical, also shaded in various tones of gray. Near the top of the cylinder, a small, flat lateral protrusion is visible, which is likely a gas flow adjustment lever. At the very top of the burner, there is a depiction of a narrow, slightly curved metallic tube, colored in a mix of brown and yellowish hues, with some shading to indicate cylindrical form. The entire object is positioned in the middle of a faintly outlined rectangular border. There is no background scenery or additional objects; the focus remains solely on the burner itself.
title: Candlestick
